gbm_population_evidence.quote: Newly diagnosed (i.e., within 6 weeks), histologically or molecularly confirmed glioblastoma or diffuse midline glioma.

candidate_evidence.quote: All subjects will receive ferumoxytol and pharmacologic ascorbate in addition to the standard treatment.

candidate_flag.reason: Candidates are IV pharmacologic ascorbate (licensed medicine also sold as supplement; manual 1.2 requires uncertain) and ferumoxytol (iron replacement product).

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Combined With Concomitant Temozolomide and External Beam Radiation Therapy for Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma

role_evidence.quote: Pharmacological ascorbate (other names: ASCOR, vitamin C, ascorbic acid): Intravenous ascorbate

agents.drug_class_hint: vitamin C given intravenously at pharmacological doses

flag.reason: Licensed medicine also sold as supplement, given IV at pharmacological dose (manual 1.2).

role_evidence.quote: Number of Ferumoxytol-related Dose Limiting Toxicities (DLTs): The recommended dose will be determined by incidence of dose limiting toxicities.

agents.drug_class_hint: iron oxide nanoparticle iron replacement product

role_evidence.quote: It is a standard-of-care treatment for GBM.

coder_notes: Diffuse midline glioma also eligible, so mixed. G6PD deficiency exclusion is a germline safety marker, not recorded. Ascorbate formulation flagged new_route (IV) as a judgement; could be none. Ferumoxytol dose-schedule differs between cohorts; primary outcome is ferumoxytol DLTs. No antitumour mechanism stated in record.
